wedge: origin/destination + party size + car fuel/toll/parking + station/terminal access + transit fares + optional time value => door-to-door trip decision showing when car vs KTX/bus actually flips for this household, not a static route article or fare lookup
last_material_result: Fresh consumer-decision discovery screened housing-fee, electricity, wedding-gift, rent-vs-jeonse and intercity transport ideas. Brokerage/electricity/wedding/rent calculators are already crowded with near-exact substitutes. Intercity transport still shows a cleaner action gap: current pages mostly compare fixed city pairs or headline fares, while household economics change materially with party size, first/last-mile access, parking and time. The strongest first survivor is a door-to-door car vs KTX/bus total-cost comparator. Existing route articles confirm the party-size crossover effect but generally stop short of a reusable household-specific decision tool.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Monetization candidates: travel/parking/rental-car affiliate, ads, or cross-promotion. Value is consumer money/time saved rather than direct subscription. Revenue remains unproven; first test should target high-intent route searches and compare CTR/action intent before any build.
next_checkpoint: Next Lane B run: validate distribution/search gap for 3 representative high-volume trip archetypes and test whether a reusable door-to-door comparator is materially different from static route articles. Check free data feasibility for tolls, fares and access-cost inputs; if exact live data would force paid APIs or platform dependence, simplify to user-input/default assumptions or KILL.
recommendation: KEEP in ASSESS as first fresh survivor. Do not BUILD yet. Prioritize evidence that the reusable household-specific crossover decision is not already commoditized.
